- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >35.0), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward — overreacts to volatility.
- Model shows persistent upward bias in the 10–20 day window, suggesting failure to account for mean reversion or short-term volatility dampening.
- Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the 15–25 day range — model is slow to adjust to new information.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in the 20–30 day window, especially when prices are trending upward — fails to capture momentum or policy-driven spikes.
- Model exhibits “smoothness bias” — overly linear or gradual changes, missing abrupt reversals or sharp corrections.
- When true price exceeds 40.0, model often fails to adjust downward, suggesting underweighting of supply/demand shocks or policy interventions.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices, leading to persistent overestimation when recent history is dominated by elevated values.
